current.text: He moved from Toronto to the Lakers this offseason.
He projects as the Lakers' sixth man. He would play power forward and backup center behind Walker Kessler. The projected starters are Doncic, Reaves, Grimes, Thybulle and Kessler.
The backup center job is still open, with Kevon Looney the other option. JJ Redick's rotation choices are unclear.
His minutes should go up from last season. Even off the bench, he could play about 27 minutes.

He is unlikely to play 31 minutes, so a Yahoo ADP of 119 is a little high. At 26 to 27 minutes he is a 14-team league player. Not starting limits his value. He went for 4 USD in an expert mock auction.
He is worth a late-round flyer or stash. If Kessler gets hurt, he would play 30+ minutes.
The Lakers have the second most back-to-backs in the league. Their playoff schedule is 3-4-3 with a March 28 end, which is in the bottom half of the league.

durable.text: He is a good shooter. His offense depends on three-point volume and efficiency.
Experts call him a bad defender. One calls him very overrated as a player, with basically one skill.
Last season was his only one in a regular rotation role. He was barely a factor in the playoffs.
Threes are his best category for a forward or center. His blocks are low for a big.

note: Yahoo ranks him 129th, near the edge of our 144-player pool. He is valued at 3 USD on Yahoo and went for 4 USD in an expert mock, so treat him as a 1 to 3 USD final-roster stash, not a target. His threes from the frontcourt make him a mild fit for builds that want 3PM from a big, but his blocks are low for his position and the Lakers have a weak playoff schedule. Early in the season, check whether he plays 26 to 27 minutes and holds the backup center job over Looney, and watch Kessler's health, since an injury to Kessler would push him past 30 minutes.
